title: Grateful Dead Live at San Diego International Sports Arena on 1973-11-14

ai_review.summary: Clean soundboard recording of a late‑1973 Hollister show, spotlighted by a scorching China > Rider and an epic The Other One sandwich.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its high‑energy second set – a triple‑sandwich of The Other One with Big River, Eyes of the World and Wharf Rat – and standout moments like China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider.  The SBD source is described as bright and clear, though reviewers note channel swapping and the need for modest pitch correction.  Overall the show is considered one of ’73’s best despite a slightly tired feel early on.

ai_rating.rationale: All four reviews give five‑star ratings and consistently praise both the musical performance and the improved soundboard quality; minor technical quirks keep the rating just below perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers call the SBD "cleaner and brighter" and the clearest available, but mention switched channels, occasional pitch‑correction needs (≈-1% to -3%) and patched audio gaps from other sources.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
The Other One (triple sandwich with Big River & Eyes of the World)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is solid but uneven, featuring a hot "Big Railroad" and decent mid‑set moments; the second set flows brilliantly with seamless transitions despite one reviewer noting the Eyes → Other One return felt premature.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for an angular, almost ’76‑style approach on China Cat Sunflower and strong lead work in the later minutes of Eyes of the World.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass shines during The Other One sandwich, adding drive that “smokes” alongside the guitars.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals are highlighted as a major strength – "great singing throughout" with standout phrasing on Black Throated Wind, Truckin' and Saturday Night; his rhythm guitar also noted as solid on Brown‑Eyed Women.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboards receive compliments for tight playing on Brown‑Eyed Women and the climactic sections of Eyes of the World.
